brief: GS's US vol color note argues sentiment and positioning have deteriorated sharply even though the S&P 500 is under 1% from highs and the Nasdaq is making new highs. The GS Monetary Policy Optimism factor fell to -8, near record lows; L/S net leverage fell a third straight week to 46.4% (2nd percentile); the fundamental L/S ratio fell to 1.57 (1st percentile); CFTC data show non-dealers sold $68bn of SPX futures in five of the last six weeks; the Sentiment Indicator logged a fifth straight negative reading. Despite that, equity vol has not followed: the Vol Panic Index is sub 2/10 and VVIX vs HYG implied vol hit a 3+ year low, so the market is not pricing credit/rates stress spilling into equities. GS argues dovish Fed speak plus a weak jobs report should calm vol and let indices reach escape velocity into earnings, and calls QQQ upside too cheap. Tech was the only sector net bought in September (still 25th percentile L/S). Iran remains the largest overhang; a relief scenario gives Nasdaq 7.5% upside, and GS bought QQQ November calls. Consensus Q3 EPS growth of 27% y/y is the highest since 2021 but decelerates from Q2's 33%; GS sees no slowdown signal and expects another above-consensus quarter, with the top 10 stocks driving over two-thirds of growth.
